harmfulness.reason: The core steps are safe for a root-rot plant: "Check the roots," "Cut away any mushy roots," and "empty any water sitting in the outer pot." No chemicals are recommended. One minor risk is the line "Peace lilies droop when thirsty, so they tell you when they need water," since drooping here is caused by rot and could prompt more watering. There is also no mention that peace lilies are toxic to pets and children, though this matters little for the advice given.

specificity_accuracy.reason: The diagnosis "probably overwatering and root rot" matches the confirmed problem. It is backed by case-specific photo evidence: "collapsing into dark brown-black, soft-looking tissue" and a "decorative cachepot without visible drainage." This echoes the reference's warning about a catch pot full of water. It does not offer the reference's water-propagation option, though it suggests "rooting healthy divisions." Some padding is generic, such as the light, fertilizer, and filtered-water advice.

feasibility.reason: Every step uses common household items: "clean scissors or pruners," "fresh, well-draining potting mix," and "perlite or orchid bark." The instructions are numbered, concrete and quick to do, e.g. "Slide the plant out of the pot" and "lift the nursery pot out of the decorative one." A home owner can do all of it this week.

generic_phrases: Hold off on fertilizer until new growth appears
Use filtered or rainwater if your tap water is high in salts or fluoride
Water only when the top 1–2 inches of soil are dry
